research_question: Can a clinician-supervised transdiagnostic model improve treatment matching and durability for heterogeneous psychiatric presentations?

population.unit_of_inference: patient nested in site and treatment pathway
population.design: prospective cohort with randomized treatment comparison where equipoise and ethics permit

feature_layers: network connectivity and reproducible graph summaries
repeated inflammatory, endocrine, or autonomic measures
time-stamped response, tolerability, adherence, and clinician risk monitoring
primary_endpoint: held-out clinical utility at a fixed decision horizon

equations.trajectory: Y[i,t,d] = alpha[d] + u[i,d] + beta[a,d] + gamma[d]'X[i] + rho[a,d]'M[i] + tau[d]t + omega[a,d]t + epsilon[i,t,d]
equations.response: logit P(R[i,t]=1) = theta0 + theta[a] + thetaX'X[i] + thetaM'M[i] + thetaT'H[i,t] + theta[aM]'(a x M[i])
equations.policy_utility: U(a|x[t]) = p_resp(a|x[t]) B_resp - p_harm(a|x[t]) C_harm - B_burden(a) - lambda Uncertainty(a|x[t])

analysis_sequence: lock feature timestamps and prevent post-decision leakage
estimate mechanism strata and treatment interactions
fit repeated-response trajectory and adaptive policy models
validate by held-out site, time period, subgroup, and missingness pattern
evaluate decision utility, safety, calibration, and overrides
run simulation-based recovery and sensitivity analyses
falsification: no reproducible gain over the symptom-dimensional baseline
mechanism strata fail stability or transportability
early updating does not improve response prediction
adaptive use worsens calibration, burden, or subgroup equity
predictive gain does not translate into clinical utility
safety_constraints: no autonomous prescription, discontinuation, or neuromodulation
clinician authorization is required for treatment changes
high-risk signals use established clinical procedures
model pause rule for safety or equity signals
